# wellr

A set of *tidy* utilities for working with plate based data. Wet-lab
experiments are often carried out in microplates of varying sizes.
[wellr](https://github.com/bradyajohnston/wellr) aims to provide a
cleaner interface to working with data from plate readers that works
well within the [tidyverse](https://tidyverse.tidyverse.org) [design
principles](https://design.tidyverse.org/unifying.html).

[wellr](https://github.com/bradyajohnston/wellr) provides a consistent
and reliable interface for dealing with plate-based data and related
calculations. It provides functions for reading the output of various
plate readers, indexing through and reformatting microtitre plates,
converting between well IDs (“C05”) and their respective rows, columns
and index.

## Installation

### From R-Universe:

This is the recommended way to install the package - as it requires no
additional dependencies. It is currently not available on CRAN.

``` r

install.packages("wellr", repos = "bradyajohnston.r-universe.dev")
```

### From GitHub

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("bradyajohnston/wellr")
```

## Basic Examples

``` r

library(wellr)

well_format("G8")
#> [1] "G08"
well_to_col_num("G8")
#> [1] 8
well_to_row_num("G8")
#> [1] 7
well_to_index("H1")
#> [1] 85
well_to_index("H1", colwise = TRUE)
#> [1] 8
well_from_index(37)
#> <well<96>[1]>
#> [1] D01
well_from_index(37, colwise = TRUE)
#> <well<96>[1]>
#> [1] E05
well_join(3, 8)
#> [1] "C08"
well_join("E", 10)
#> [1] "E10"
```

## Well IDs that know their plate

Well IDs returned by wellr are
[`well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
vectors: they print, compare and join like the character vectors they
are underneath, but also record the size of the plate they come from.
Conversions use it automatically, so a 384 well plate is indexed
correctly without saying so.

``` r

x <- well(c("a1", "B2", "p24"), plate = 384)
x
#> <well<384>[3]>
#> [1] A01 B02 P24

x == "B02"
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
well_to_index(x)
#> [1]   1  26 384
well_plate_size(x)
#> [1] 384
```

Use [`as.character()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html) to get a
plain character vector.

## Reading Biotek

Get the file paths of the demo files.

``` r

file_data <- system.file("extdata",
  "20220929_1steptimer20.csv",
  package = "wellr"
)

file_meta <- system.file("extdata",
  "20220929_1steptimer20_metainfo.csv",
  package = "wellr"
)
```

Read in an example plate from a Biotek plate reader.

``` r

plate <- plate_read_biotek(file_data)
plate
#> # A tibble: 19,200 × 4
#>     time well         lum od600
#>    <dbl> <well:384> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1  358. A01            3 0.09 
#>  2  358. A02           27 0.097
#>  3  358. A03            4 0.091
#>  4  358. A04            3 0.09 
#>  5  358. A05           32 0.096
#>  6  358. A06            3 0.097
#>  7  358. A07           78 0.094
#>  8  358. A08            2 0.095
#>  9  358. A09           20 0.095
#> 10  358. A10          103 0.093
#> # ℹ 19,190 more rows
```

``` r

plate |>
  plate_add_meta(file_meta)
#> # A tibble: 19,200 × 8
#>     time well         lum od600 strain  concentration promoter rbs  
#>    <dbl> <well:384> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>           <dbl> <chr>    <chr>
#>  1  358. A01            3 0.09  <NA>               NA <NA>     <NA> 
#>  2  358. A02           27 0.097 pRW0041             0 PJ23100  wk2  
#>  3  358. A03            4 0.091 pRW0044             0 PJ23107  wk2  
#>  4  358. A04            3 0.09  pRW0046             0 PJ23109  wk2  
#>  5  358. A05           32 0.096 pRW0047             0 PJ23110  wk2  
#>  6  358. A06            3 0.097 pRW0048             0 PJ23111  wk2  
#>  7  358. A07           78 0.094 pRW0053             0 PJ23100  st8  
#>  8  358. A08            2 0.095 pRW0056             0 PJ23107  st8  
#>  9  358. A09           20 0.095 pRW0058             0 PJ23109  st8  
#> 10  358. A10          103 0.093 pRW0059             0 PJ23110  st8  
#> # ℹ 19,190 more rows
```

### Read Biotek Wavelength Data

If the biotek `.csv` file includes spectral readings from different
wavelengths, these won’t be included in the regular
[`plate_read_biotek()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_biotek.md)
function’s output - as they don’t have associated time information.

The
[`plate_read_biotek_wl()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_biotek_wl.md)
function extracts these readings, and the resulting data frame includes
a `id` column, specifying which wavelength reading they come from.

``` r

file_including_wavelength <- system.file(
  "extdata", "2024-02-29_vio_GFP_main.csv",
  package = "wellr"
)

plate_read_biotek(file_including_wavelength)
#> # A tibble: 14,304 × 7
#>     time well      od600 gfp_485 vio_575 vio_585 vio_595
#>    <dbl> <well:96> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1  469. A01       0.041     260   0.042   0.041   0.041
#>  2  469. A02       0.043     258   0.044   0.044   0.043
#>  3  469. A03       0.043     258   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  4  469. A04       0.044     254   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  5  469. A05       0.044     256   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  6  469. A06       0.043     255   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  7  469. A07       0.043     244   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  8  469. A08       0.045     252   0.045   0.045   0.045
#>  9  469. A09       0.045     251   0.045   0.045   0.045
#> 10  469. A10       0.045     247   0.045   0.046   0.045
#> # ℹ 14,294 more rows
```

If reading in fluorescent data, there will sometimes be two wavelengths
reported in the `.csv`. By default just the first wavelength will be
used for the column names, but you can ensure that both wavelengths are
included by useing `second_wl = TRUE`. The `gfp` column now includes the
second wavelength that the fluorescence was measured at.

``` r

plate_read_biotek(file_including_wavelength, second_wl = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 14,304 × 7
#>     time well      od600 gfp_485_530 vio_575 vio_585 vio_595
#>    <dbl> <well:96> <dbl>       <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1  469. A01       0.041         260   0.042   0.041   0.041
#>  2  469. A02       0.043         258   0.044   0.044   0.043
#>  3  469. A03       0.043         258   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  4  469. A04       0.044         254   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  5  469. A05       0.044         256   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  6  469. A06       0.043         255   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  7  469. A07       0.043         244   0.044   0.044   0.044
#>  8  469. A08       0.045         252   0.045   0.045   0.045
#>  9  469. A09       0.045         251   0.045   0.045   0.045
#> 10  469. A10       0.045         247   0.045   0.046   0.045
#> # ℹ 14,294 more rows
```

When reading the spectral data from the file, the readings do not
include time data.

The resulting data frame will however include a `id` column with
`id = 1` being the first reading, `id = 2` being the second reading etc.

``` r

plate_read_biotek_wl(file_including_wavelength)
#> # A tibble: 23,616 × 4
#>    id    wavelength well      value
#>    <chr>      <dbl> <well:96> <dbl>
#>  1 1            300 A01       0.28 
#>  2 1            300 A02       0.284
#>  3 1            300 A03       0.285
#>  4 1            300 A04       0.285
#>  5 1            300 A05       0.285
#>  6 1            300 A06       0.284
#>  7 1            300 A07       0.275
#>  8 1            300 A08       0.279
#>  9 1            300 A09       0.282
#> 10 1            300 A10       0.28 
#> # ℹ 23,606 more rows
```

## Creating Dummy Plates

Create a data frame for plate-based data.

``` r

well_plate(8, 12)
#> # A tibble: 96 × 3
#>      row   col well     
#>    <int> <int> <well:96>
#>  1     1     1 A01      
#>  2     1     2 A02      
#>  3     1     3 A03      
#>  4     1     4 A04      
#>  5     1     5 A05      
#>  6     1     6 A06      
#>  7     1     7 A07      
#>  8     1     8 A08      
#>  9     1     9 A09      
#> 10     1    10 A10      
#> # ℹ 86 more rows
```

## Helpful Plotting Functions

``` r

set.seed(3)
plate <- well_plate(8, 12)[, "well"]
plate$value <- rnorm(96, sd = 10)

well_plot(plate, well, value)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-10-1.png)

# Package index

## Plate Functions

Functions for working with plates

- [`plate_add_meta()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_add_meta.md)
  :

  Add `{plater{` Formatted Metadata to a Dataset

- [`plate_read_biotek()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_biotek.md)
  : Read Biotek Output CSV Files

- [`plate_read_biotek_wl()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_biotek_wl.md)
  :

  Read the `wavelength` data blocks from a *biotek* `.csv` file.

- [`plate_read_meta()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_meta.md)
  :

  Read a [plater](https://docs.ropensci.org/plater/) Formatted Metadata
  File

- [`plate_read_tecan()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/plate_read_tecan.md)
  : Read the output of Tecan Plate Readers

## Well Functions

Functions for formatting and manipulating well-related properties.

- [`well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`as_well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`is_well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`well_plate_size()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`well_plate_dims()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  : Well IDs that know their plate
- [`well_check()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_check.md)
  : Checks if a well ID contains a letter and a number in the correct
  format.
- [`well_df_to_mat()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_df_to_mat.md)
  : Convert a data.frame to a Matrix in Plate Format
- [`well_df_to_mat_frames()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_df_to_mat_frames.md)
  : Convert a DataFrame to a Multi-Frame Matrix
- [`well_dis()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_dis.md)
  : Relative Distance Between Given Well and a Reference Row
- [`well_dis_plate()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_dis_plate.md)
  : Relative Distance for an Entire Plate
- [`well_format()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_format.md)
  : Format a Well to Uppercase and Padded Numbers
- [`well_from_index()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_from_index.md)
  : Convert Numeric Index to Well ID.
- [`well_join()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_join.md)
  : Join a row and column into a well ID.
- [`well_mat_frames_to_df()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_mat_frames_to_df.md)
  : Turn a Multi-Frame Matrix into a DataFrame
- [`well_mat_to_df()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_mat_to_df.md)
  : Convert a Plate Matrix to a DataFrame
- [`well_plate()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_plate.md)
  : Create a Tibble of Plate Information
- [`well_plot()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_plot.md)
  : Plot a Plate Map
- [`well_reorder_df()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_reorder_df.md)
  : Reorder a Plate-Based DataFrame
- [`well_row()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_row.md)
  [`well_col()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_row.md)
  : Rows and columns of a plate
- [`well_to_col_num()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_to_col_num.md)
  : Extract number from well ID.
- [`well_to_index()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_to_index.md)
  : Converts Well ID to a Numeric Index
- [`well_to_row_let()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_to_row_let.md)
  : Extracts letter from well ID.
- [`well_to_row_num()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well_to_row_num.md)
  : Convert Well ID to Row Number

## Reading Files

reading of different metadata and plate data files.

- [`read_meta()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/read_meta.md)
  :

  Read a [plater](https://docs.ropensci.org/plater/) formatted metadata
  file

## Utilities

Utility tests for dealing with plate metadata.

- [`is_well_id()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/is_well_id.md)
  : Logical test for well ID format.
- [`well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`as_well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`is_well()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`well_plate_size()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  [`well_plate_dims()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/wellr/reference/well.md)
  : Well IDs that know their plate
